_: The five findings of the red (Screening) hero, in the EXACT keys lot S1 declared (message of the night of 5 to 6). Provenance: every figure in a/b/cote is a cell of ~/Documents/cascade-screening/releve-public.json at seal `sceau`; S1 refuses to build if the record on disk no longer matches that seal, and this file names each figure's cell in `source` beside it: {table, palier, seuil, mesure} reads releve[table].tables[palier][seuil][mesure] ({succes, n, taux, bas, haut}); {table, compte} reads releve[table][compte]. `source` is provenance for reviewers and future guards; builders may ignore it. Intervals in legends are Wilson 95% from the same cells, en dash, never an em dash. The rule behind finding 03 is the tool's own default (optimise: Wilson lower bound of recall >= 0.90, then the fewest false alerts), the same rule the live instrument applies: one rule on the whole site, chosen, not measured, and said on the fiche. `annotations` are fractions of the rendered tower box (anchor x, anchor y, label x, label y, text), placed by the chef on the rendered states.

findings.titre: Exact matching raises no false alert and finds few confirmed matches.
findings.phrase: The tool keeps the settings that catch at least 90% of true matches, then takes the fewest false alerts. Exact matching catches 21.7% and raises no false alert on the 60 pairs of near-matches.
findings.leg_a: recall, the share of true matches found: 21.7% on 60 pairs of confirmed matches, interval 13% to 34%
findings.leg_b: false alerts 0% on 60 pairs of near-matches, interval 0% to 6%
findings.rail: Exact matching: 21.7% recall, no false alert

findings.titre: Jaro-winkler at 0.50 finds every match and alerts on most non-matches.
findings.phrase: Jaro-winkler at threshold 0.50 finds every one of the 60 pairs of confirmed matches, and alerts on 85% of the 60 pairs of near-matches.
findings.leg_a: recall 100% for jaro-winkler at 0.50, interval 94% to 100%, 60 pairs of matches
findings.leg_b: false alerts 85% at the same cell, interval 74% to 92%, 60 pairs of near-matches

findings.titre: Catching almost every true match costs a great many false alerts.
findings.phrase: This setting finds 98.3% of the true matches. It also flags 76.7% of the near-matches, which were written to be hard to tell apart. Your own alerts will give your own rate.
findings.leg_a: recall 98.3% for jaro-winkler at 0.56, interval 91% to 100%, 60 pairs of matches
findings.leg_b: false alerts 76.7% at the same cell, interval 65% to 86%, 60 pairs of near-matches

findings.titre: The best cell scores 17.2% false alerts on generated pairs against 76.7% on written pairs.
findings.phrase: The same cell reads 76.7% false alerts on the 60 pairs of near-matches we wrote and 17.2% on the 360 pairs we generated. The generated set is easier, so the tool measures it separately and the headline rate does not include it.
findings.leg_a: false alerts 76.7% at the best cell on 60 pairs of near-matches we wrote, interval 65% to 86%
findings.leg_b: false alerts 17.2% at the same cell on 360 pairs of generated near-matches, interval 14% to 21%
findings.rail: Generated pairs, kept separate from the written ones

findings.titre: Measure the whole sweep on your own alert history.
findings.phrase: Every rate here comes from our public test set: 60 pairs of confirmed matches and 60 pairs of near-matches, written by us, and another 360 pairs of each kind, generated. Run it once on your own alert history and the report is written next to your file.
findings.leg_a: 60 pairs of confirmed matches and 60 pairs of near-matches, written by us, behind the rates
findings.leg_b: another 360 pairs of each kind, generated under a seed, and kept separate
